newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Litigation explosion seen hitting Asia insurers.
newsitem.headline: Litigation explosion seen hitting Asia insurers.

text.p: A litigation explosion could hit Asia's insurance markets by the turn of the century, mirroring the trend of escalating disputes between insured and insurer in the U.S. and Europe, a lawyer said on Monday.
"It'll be here within two or three years," R. Mark Keenan, a partner with U.S. law firm Anderson Kill & Olick, told Reuters.

"I don't know necessarily that there will be that mass tort type claim where every smoker sues every tobacco company or manufacturer in the area, but I believe litigation problems (in Asia) will happen very quickly," Keenan said.
He said commercial contract disputes and personal lines liability claims would be the key drivers of litigation.
Huge payouts characterise product liability litigation in the U.S., and Asians could be expected to follow this route into the litigation quagmire, laywers say.
"There's a fear that product liability claims in Asia are being driven by 'a get rich quick' motive," said one attorney who declined to be identified.
Keenan said the potential for dispute was escalating in tandem with the rapid expansion of the insurance market in Asia.

Insurers -- particularly foreign players seeking a slice of the business in the world's most vibrant market -- have slashed rates to secure market sharem and analysts believe they have accumulated many of the worst risks in the region.
The accumulation of bad risks at low rates could provide the spark to the powder keg of litigation when the claims eventually begin to roll in, Keenan warned.
"All it would take is one catastrophic loss where there is non-payment," he said.
